specials.description: The Cursed Hillman has had to learn to survive in the bleak wilderness of the Empire. As such, he is incredibly skilled with his bow. He may move at half-rate, and still fire his bow without penalty.

specials.name: Thin Flesh
specials.description: Due to his constant changing into lupine form and back, his flesh has weakened to ease the transformation. As such, he counts as having -1T in hand to hand combat.

specials.name: Lycanthrope
specials.description: The Cursed Hillman is a werewolf. Any time he loses a wound, he must roll a D6. On a roll of 4+, the beast within escapes and he transforms into a werewolf. Ignore any injury table rolls. Should he not transform, roll on the injury table at -1 (thus knocked down is 2-3, stunned is 4-5, and OOA is on a 6 only). While in wolf-form, he has a bonus Bite attack. This is resolved at -1S.

hired_sword.unique_to: A Cursed Hillman can be hired by the Undead, Beastmen or Possessed warbands.

available_special_skills.name: Control
available_special_skills.description: So long has he been cursed that the Hillman can attempt to call upon the beast within at will. The Hillman can transform into the Werewolf during the shooting phase on a D6 roll of 2+. Should this roll fail, the Hillman must remain static as the excruciating transformation takes longer than anticipated. He counts as being knocked down, and will be completely transformed by the beginning of his controller’s next turn.

available_special_skills.name: Rage
available_special_skills.description: The Hillman calls upon his curse to imbue himself with supernatural powers. He gains +1WS, +1S, +1I and an extra attack as his off-hand has transformed into a claw. This skill can only be taken if the Control skill is already chosen.

name: Dark Mage
description: Hedge Wizard, Warlock, Witch; all of these are used to describe those who are touched with the gift. The Dark Mage treads a different path than those typically associated with these titles, however. Bent on the destruction of Necromancy, the Dark Mage practices the true dark arts, and treats them with the respect they deserve.

specials.name: Wizard
specials.description: The Dark Mage is a wizard, and may randomly generate a spell from the Dark Magic list, and may gain more spells from that or from the Lesser Magic list found in the Core Rulebook.

specials.name: Despise Despoilers
specials.description: A Dark Mage Hates Necromancers, and anyone who casts spells from the Necromancy or the Dreaded Scrolls of Nagash.

specials.name: Self Assured
specials.description: Dark Mages are immune to the effects of All Alone tests and will never flee as a result.

spells.name: 1 - Banishment
spells.description: Difficulty 8. Pulling the energies of death to him, the Dark Mage dispels the power of the undead. All Undead within 4” of the Dark Mage must take an unmodified Leadership Test or suffer a S4 hit.

spells.name: 2 - Soul Render
spells.description: Difficulty 8. For the most brief of moments, the Mage centers dark energies upon an unlucky foe. Soul Render is a magic missile spell, with a range of 18 inches. If successfully cast, the spell causes D3 S3 hits.

spells.name: 3 - Shade Mount
spells.description: Difficulty 8. Darkness forms about the caster, carrying him aloft on wings of shadow. This spell may be cast on the wizard himself, or a hero within 8 inches of him. Upon a successful casting, the model may immediately fly up to 12 inches. Should this movement bring the model into Base to Base contact with an enemy model, consider it a charge.

spells.name: 4 - Jozun’s Decay
spells.description: Difficulty 9. Ashes and dust. Focusing the dark energies, the wizard forces the very life from his opponent. This spell has a range of 12 inches. Upon a successful casting, the target must pass a Leadership Test, or suffer a one point reduction to its Toughness attribute. Each recovery phase the model must attempt to pass a Leadership Test, reducing its Toughness a further point for each failure. Should a model be reduced to 0 Toughness, it is removed from the game irrespective of how many wounds it has left. Should a Leadership Test be passed, the model must play the remainder of the game at its modified Toughness score. A model may not be targeted more than once per game.

spells.name: 5 - Cowel of Pain
spells.description: Difficulty 6. Nothing compares to the pain of the dark. Wrapping it about him like a cloak, the caster strengthens himself. The mage cannot be Stunned until his next magic phase. Treat 3-4 results as Knocked Down instead.

spells.name: 6 - Doom & Dark
spells.description: Difficulty 7. Dark energies coalesce about the mage, chilling the air and driving dread into all those around him. Any model within 2” of the Dark Mage must take an immediate All Alone Test, even if in close combat. Should a model flee from Close Combat, free strikes occur as normal, assuming that there are combatants who have not failed their test.

hired_sword.unique_to: Human Mercs, “Good” aligned warbands. May not be hired by any Undead, Sisters of Sigmar or Witch Hunters.

name: Dwarf Slayer Pirate
description:
In the ancient Dwarf stronghold of Barak-Varr is a great trade center, and many Dwarf merchant ships make port in its harbors. The crew of these ships are some of the most cunning and skilled sailors in the old world. It is their charge not only to man the ships but also to protect the precious cargo of those ships, often rare Dwarven ales and treasures.
Should one of these shipments be lost, whether captured, wrecked, or lost to the depths of the sea, a great dishonor is placed on both captain and crew of the ship. This shame is often too much to bear, and occasionally such a Dwarf seaman will undertake the Slayer Oath, but will retain his old habits and combat preferences to those of the traditional troll slayers.
The Slayer Pirate “hired guns” will often turn to the city of the damned to seek out an honorable death in combat.

specials.name: Deathwish
specials.description: It is the goal of the Slayer Pirates to die in combat and they are therefore immune to psychology and will never need to test if fighting alone.

specials.name: Hard to Kill
specials.description: Dwarfs are tough, resilient individuals who are only taken out of action on an injury roll of 6. Treat a roll of 5 as stunned instead.

specials.name: Hard Head
specials.description: Dwarf Slayer Pirates ignore the concussion special rule, they are not easy to knock out!

specials.name: Festooned with Pistols
specials.description: Dwarf Slayer Pirates carry so many pistols into battle that they never have to reload, they always have a new pistol primed and ready to fire. The only exception is hand-to-hand combat. The Slayer Pirate will not have time to draw a new pistol every round of hand-to-hand combat, he may only use pistols in the first round. In subsequent rounds of hand-to-hand combat the pistol should be counted as a club. He may draw another pistol once he is out of combat or all of his opponents are knocked down or stunned.

specials.name: Raging Drunk
specials.description: The combination of being a Dwarf and spending the better part of life on the sea means Slayer Pirates usually know where to acquire some fine Dwarven Ale. A warband including a Slayer Pirate treats Bugman's Ale as Rare 6, but must pay an extra 2d6 gold crowns to compensate for the copious amounts of ale that the Slayer Pirate will consume.

hired_sword.unique_to: Mercenaries, Averlanders, Ostlanders, Kislevites, Witch Hunters, Tileans, Dwarf Treasure Hunters, Bandits, and Pirates

name: Emissary of Chaos
description: From the northern wastes they come, the mortal voices of the gods of chaos. They flock to Mordheim, for here Chaos rules supreme and the dark powers reward the faithful.

specials.name: Special Skills
specials.description: An Emissary of Chaos's special skills depend on which god he serves. Khorne: Frenzy, +1A. Tzeentch: Gains 1 spell from the Chaos Rituals (may cast spells while wearing armour). Nurgle: All attacks are poisoned (as black lotus), cause fear. Slaanesh: All enemies must pass a Leadership test to charge Emissary. Those that do engage the Emissary in close combat suffer a -1 to their to hit rolls.

hired_sword.unique_to: Dark Elves, Possessed, Carnival of Chaos, Norse, and Beastmen may hire an Emissary of Chaos.

name: Estalian Diestro
description: Having left their home, the Diestro converge upon Mordheim to make their fortune. It is not often that the skilled of Estalia can be found, as Estalian Diestros are some of the finest duelists in the old world, but their services do not come cheaply.

specials.name: Rapier
specials.description: The Rapier is a long thin blade commonly used by duelists. It is a deadly, sharp weapon capable of delivering multitude of blows. Range: Close Combat. Strength: As User. Special Rules: Parry, Barrage. Parry: Like all swords, you may use a rapier to parry hand-to-hand combat. Barrage: A warrior armed with a rapier rolls to hit and to wound as normal. However, if you manage to hit your opponent but fail to wound you may attack again just as if you had another attack but at –1 to hit (down to a maximum of needing a ‘6’ to hit). Any additional attacks gained in this fashion also benefit from the Barrage special rule.

specials.name: Main Gauche
specials.description: Slender but of good steel, the Main Gauche is often employed by professional fighters out of Estalia. Perfectly balanced, they spin about in their wielder's hand, striking and parrying blows alike. Range: Close Combat. Strength: As User. The main gauche is a special dagger, which Diestros use with their offhand (which is in most cases the left hand, hence the name). Any Estalian Diestro has the option to either use this weapon as a dagger, thus gaining an additional attack, OR to parry a blow with it as if it was a sword. In the latter case, they gain NO additional attack. The player may choose each turn in which way the fighter will use the main gauche.

hired_sword.unique_to: Anyone save for Chaotic (Possessed, Carnival, Beastmen, Skaven), Undead (of any kind), Tilean or Osterlander warbands may hire the Diestro.

name: The Fallen Sister
description: Wizards have little to say in whether the world of magic touches them or not. Even those who have devoted their life to the service of Sigmar may find themselves cursed with the gift. When this happens within the cloistered walls of a Sigmarite Abbey, the order can either execute one of its own, or let her flee. Unfortunately (for them), many flee, confused and fearful of their new-found abilities. But the life of a lone female on the mean streets of the Empire is not a safe one, which is why many have been drawn by the riches of Mordheim.

specials.name: Wizard
specials.description: A Fallen Sister has been cursed with the ability to use magic. She has one spell generated at random from the Lesser Magic list.

specials.name: Warrior Wizard
specials.description: A Fallen Sister has learned to cast her spells whilst wearing her customary armour and garb.

specials.name: Ashamed and Afraid
specials.description: A Fallen Sister has risked much in her attempts to escape the Abbey and the notice of her former sisters. She must make a Leadership test in order to charge any member of a Sisters of Sigmar warband, or a Warrior-Priest from a Witch Hunters warband.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband except Skaven, Undead, Witch Hunters or Sisters of Sigmar may hire a Fallen Sister.

name: Goblin Lantern Bearer
description: It's tough being a goblin, especially if you feel you have talent. The orcs don't take you seriously, the other goblins pick on you, and no one trusts you. So what's a goblin to do? Why, strike out on your own of course! Armed with nothing but a lantern and a dagger, this plucky little greenskin is ready to light the way through the darkest ruins of Mordheim.

specials.name: Smart (for a Goblin)
specials.description: The Goblin Lantern Bearer has survived partially on his brains. Being one of the smarter from the litter, he does not suffer from animosity as most goblins do.

specials.name: Very Lucky
specials.description: The Goblin Lantern Bearer has survived for some time by his luck. If the goblin is taken out of action during the game, roll for his injuries with the following results: 1 – Lost. 2-6 – Survives.

specials.name: Small Size
specials.description: Due to their small size, Goblin Lantern Bearers can fit into very small spaces. If the goblin is not taken out of action during the fight, then they can help in the search for wyrdstone. When rolling for wyrdstone, roll dice as normal for the warband. The Goblin Lantern Bearer adds +3 to the total dice roll when determining the number of shards found (i.e. if the dice total is 15, then add +3 for a total of 18, and thus 4 shards found instead of 3).

name: Gravesman
description: Welcome to Crazy Grom's. Nowhere else in Mordheim will you find a better assortment of hirelings. If you don't find what you're looking for, then you're not going to find it anywhere! There is never a shortage of bodies in Mordheim, and thus there is never a shortage of work for the gravesmen. Disease and pestilence run rampant in the city-proper, but along the outer skirts of Mordheim where the temporary settlements and encampments of those daring or foolish lie, a certain level of order must be maintained.

specials.name: He’s o’er dere
specials.description: A Gravesman knows what’s worth saving. Should a Hero die (rolls 11-15 on the Serious Injuries Chart post-game) you may retain his equipment on a D6 roll of 4+ thanks to the Gravesman’s instinctive greed. This occurs only if you pay the Gravesman’s upkeep; if you do not, he keeps what he has found.

hired_sword.unique_to: Anyone save for Undead (of any kind), or Carnival of Chaos warbands may hire the Gravesman.

name: Halfling Knight
description: While few and far between as they are, it is not unheard of for a halfling to strive for a little more renown than their kin. These brave (or foolish) halflings take up arms and mount their faithful hounds, riding into battle with all the courage of a knight of the realm, if not quite the same stature.

specials.name: Slay Large Creature
specials.description: A Halfling Knight, when charging a Large sized creature, gains +1S (this is in addition to the +1S he gains simply for charging with a cavalry spear).

hired_sword.unique_to: Any good aligned warband may hire a Halfling Knight.

name: Imperial Tactician
description: The Empire is famed for its superior generals and expert field commanders. When not in war, these same tacticians can be found offering their services to those who can afford them, bringing their strategic genius to the streets of Mordheim.

specials.name: Expert Tactician
specials.description: At the start of the game, after all warbands have been deployed, the Imperial Tactician may then recommend up to D3+1 changes to your deployment (IE, you may change the starting position of up to D3+1 of your warriors).

specials.name: Read the Battle
specials.description: As the Imperial Tactician has an eye for reading how any battle is going, he knows when a cause is lost or not. As long as the Imperial Tactician is not out of action, the hiring warband automatically passes the first rout test they are required to make.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any human warband may hire an Imperial Tactician.

available_special_skills.name: Organized Search Party
available_special_skills.description: The warband may re-roll one exploration die.

available_special_skills.name: Send False Signals
available_special_skills.description: By misleading the opposing warband(s), an Imperial Tactician can make them deploy their forces in a way beneficial to his own warband. Thus, after all warbands have deployed (but before the hiring player has used the Expert Tactician ability), the player controlling the Imperial Tactician may move 1 member from each opposing warband D6” in any direction. This move may not move a warband member off the board, nor may it place a member of the warband in direct harm (you can't force a warrior to jump off a building!).

name: Knight of the White Wolf
description:
The oldest of the Templar Orders in the Empire, Knights of the White Wolf are known for their strict military discipline and ferocious fighting style. Hailing from Middenland, they are commonly adorned in gleaming armour with cloaks made of wolf-pelts, accompanied by wild hair and great beards.
Also known as White Wolves, the order dutifully serves Ar-Ulric, leader of the Cult of Ulric who collectively worships Ulric; God of Battle, Wolves, and Winter. Ulric’s religious following is one of the largest in the Empire, second only to the Cult of Sigmar.
Knights of the White Wolf are typically mounted, armed with large cavalry hammers that they swing wildly over their heads during charges. However, some are often seen on foot wielding even greater two-handed warhammers, bellowing terrifying howls at their enemies as they pledge oaths to Ulric, praying he grant them strength in battle.

specials.name: Pride of Ar-Ulric
specials.description: Infamous throughout the Empire, the White Wolves’ courage and martial prowess is nothing short of inspiring to your average warrior. Knights of the White Wolf may act as a Leader to their comrades, allowing them to use his Leadership characteristic as their own when taking Leadership tests. However, his Leadership value cannot be used for the purposes of rout tests.

specials.name: Cavalryman
specials.description: The knight has left his mount behind before venturing into the city of the damned, but will use another if the warband wishes. Knights of the White Wolf may be given a Warhorse to ride (and no lesser steed) if the warband possesses one. This will grant him the usual Warhorse bonuses and increase the warband’s rating +5 per the normal Warhorse rules.

specials.name: Among Wolves
specials.description: The Knight’s upkeep cost is halved if he is hired by a Middenheim warband, as he is obliged to work with his kin.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any Human Mercenary warband

name: Ninja Gnoblar
description:
Though for the most part glad to be the slaves of Ogres, some Gnoblars eventually find their lives too hard in the east and mass together in massive armies that travel into the known world. Gnoblars have many sub-species, commonly known by their attributes, such as Wyrdstone Gnoblar, Lookout Gnoblar, Luck Gnoblar, Gnoblar-Blood-Gnoblars, Boglars, Toad-Gnoblars among others.
Most people simply ignore gnoblars because they have bigger problems in their hands (the least not being the Ogres!), but this little git is not to be sneered at. Having spent some time spying the Celestial Dragon Monks of far east, this Gnoblar has some muscle to add in a fight!

specials.name: Stealthy
specials.description: The Ninja Gnoblar can throw his shurikens while hidden without revealing his position to the enemy. The target model can take an Initiative test in order to try to spot the throwing Ninja. If the test is successful, the Gnoblar no longer counts as hidden.

specials.name: Rooftop to Rooftop
specials.description: The Ninja Gnoblar is skilled in jumping over streets and gaps. He doesn't deduct the distance jumped from his movement. This means he can run 8" and still jump the 3".

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband except Ogres and warbands with fear-causing creatures

available_special_skills.name: Expert Rooftop Jumper
available_special_skills.description: The Ninja is even more skilled in jumping on the roofs. He may jump up to 4" and may re-roll a failed Initiative test when jumping or making a diving charge.

name: Ogre Slave Master
description: As of men, Ogre's too have fallen to the dark and corrupt ways of evil. Certain ruthless Ogre's have been recruited by the forces of chaos to serve as slave masters, driving captured prisoners before them into battle or keeping them chained for later sale.

specials.name: Slave Master
specials.description: Slave Master works much the same as the Bounty Hunter, except that the "mark" becomes owned by the Slave Master at the end of a battle. (No reward money is earnt, as you would from the Bounty Hunter Skill, you just now own the "mark"), but gets the D3 experience if he survives and the warband has won as normal. Thus the "mark" now works for the Slave Master's warband and will always be within 8" of him (thanks to a mighty big chain shackled to the "mark" and held by the Slave Master). If the Slave Master is holding the shackles he can only use one weapon. The "mark's" weapons can be kept or sold depending on what the Slave Master warband player wants to do. If the Slave Master is taken OOA in a battle and none of the Slave Master's warband members are within 8" of the "mark", then the "mark" will automatically run for the nearest safe area (whether that's off the board, in which case it disappears forever, or towards its original warband). If the mark ever comes within 8" of its original warband, then it automatically is controlled by the original owner of the "mark". If the Slave Master is taken OOA in a battle and the mark is within 8" of another figure from the Slave Master's warband, the "mark" will charge this closest model of that warband automatically in rage (treat as having hatred).

specials.name: Fear
specials.description: Ogres are large, threatening creatures that cause fear.

specials.name: Large Target
specials.description: Ogres are Large Targets as defined in the shooting rules.

hired_sword.unique_to: Possessed, Carnival of Chaos and Beastmen.

name: Slaver
description: While many adventurers come to Mordheim for its lost treasures and the valuable Wyrdstone, there are those who come for a different kind of prize. Slavers are ruthless individuals who capture and sell people for profit, and the chaos-torn streets of Mordheim provide plenty of opportunities.

specials.name: Slaver
specials.description: Any hero or henchman put out of action by the Slaver will automatically be Captured (as per roll 61 of the Heroes Serious Injuries Chart in the Mordheim Rulebook). Note that any hero or henchman captured must be sold. Heroes sell for D6 x10 gold crowns and Henchmen sell for D6 x3 gold crowns. If a warband cannot pay this price, then that particular hero or henchman is sold into slavery and removed from the roster.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any evil warband may hire a Slaver.

name: Swashbuckler
description: Swashbucklers live for adventure. The more risky the quest, the better. While gold is a definite bonus, a true Swashbuckler is in it for the thrill of the fight and the glory of the tale.

specials.name: Acrobatic
specials.description: As a Swashbuckler relies on their dexterity, they have extremely good balance. As such, a Swashbuckler need not make an Initiative test when he is wounded and within 1” of a building edge.

specials.name: Nimble
specials.description: A Swashbuckler is used to climbing in and out of windows, as well as running along rooftops. To reflect this, a Swashbuckler may run or charge while climbing.

specials.name: Charismatic
specials.description: Because of the Swashbuckler's sheer attractiveness, any opponent from the opposite sex (Sisters of Sigmar, Amazons), must make a Leadership test if they wish to charge him.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any non-evil warband may hire a Swashbuckler.

name: Ungor Trapper
description: In the twisted forests this lonely Ungor has kept himself alive by not only hunting the animals he has tracked down, but also by trapping unwary travellers for food and loot. His skills with a bow and his cunning traps make him a valuable, if untrustworthy, addition to any warband willing to work with such a creature.

specials.name: Set Traps
specials.description: An Ungor Trapper may set a trap if he spends a turn doing nothing else (he may not set traps if he’s just recovered from being Knocked Down). Place a marker in base contact with the Ungor Trapper. When a model, friend or foe, moves within 2" of the marker he risks setting off the trap – roll a D6. On a score of 3+ he has triggered the trap and suffers a S4 hit (note that the Ungor Trapper won’t trigger his own traps). If the trap did not wound the model or it didn’t trigger, the ‘victim’ may finish his move; otherwise he is placed Knocked Down or Stunned 2" from the marker. Regardless of whether the trap was triggered or not, the marker is removed.

specials.name: Hunter’s Eye
specials.description: The Ungor Trapper’s keen eyesight and mastery of the bow allow him to pinpoint weak points on an opponent’s body when shooting, conferring a +1 on injury rolls after a successful wound caused by shooting.

specials.name: Excellent Sight
specials.description: The Ungor Trapper spots Hidden enemies from twice as far as other warriors (i.e., twice his Initiative value in inches).

specials.name: Just a Twit
specials.description: While the Ungor’s not as fearless as his bigger conspecifics, an Ungor Trapper who has been taken Out of Action will leave the warband on a 1-3 and take 10gc upkeep with him. You may discard this rule with the Fearless skill.

hired_sword.unique_to: Beastmen, Cult of the Possessed, Norse, Marauders of Chaos.

available_special_skills.name: Mutant
available_special_skills.description: The Ungor may buy one mutation. See Mutants section on special rules.

available_special_skills.name: Fearless
available_special_skills.description: Immune to fear and all alone tests.

available_special_skills.name: Manhater
available_special_skills.description: Will be affected by the rules of hatred when fighting any Human warbands.

name: Weaponsmith
description: Armourers, blacksmiths, and ironmongers are useful elements for any warband venturing into the ruins of Mordheim; they are skilled at maintaining and improving the weapons and armour of their employers.

specials.name: Maintenance
specials.description: Every now and then, the Weaponsmith manages to get his hands on tools and spare parts with which he can make improvements to certain types of equipment, as long as they are equipped by members of your warband or are stored in your warband’s treasure. Before each game, roll 1D6 and apply the result to the equipment of your Heroes and the Weaponsmith, accepting the first result even if no model is equipped with the relevant equipment: 1: The Weaponsmith hammers a few nails, polishes a few blades, but nothing more. 2: Heavy armours provide a saving throw of 4+, light armours of 5+. 3: Helmets give a saving throw of +1 in addition to their normal effect. 4: Bucklers give a saving throw of +1 in addition to their normal effect. 5: Shields allow parrying like bucklers in addition to their normal effect. 6: Short bows, bows, crossbows, and handguns have their range increased by 6", pistols and duelling pistols by 3". This increase does not stack with other bonuses from additional skills or special rules (the highest bonus applies).

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband other than Possessed, Undead, Skaven, Carnival of Chaos, Orcs & Goblins, Beastmen, and any other “evil” warband may hire a Weaponsmith.

name: Wood Elf Hunter
description: While reclusive and wary of outsiders, it is not unheard of for one of the younger woodland elves to venture into the Empire in search of adventure. These skilled hunters bring their exceptional archery and woodcraft to the warbands that can afford their services.

specials.name: Stalk
specials.description: Such is the skill with which a Wood Elf Hunter shoots that he may remain hidden after shooting his bow on a roll of 4+.

specials.name: Hunted
specials.description: At the start of each game, the Wood Elf Hunter may choose 1 enemy to be his prey. All attacks against that enemy, be it missile or close combat, are made at +1 on the “To Hit” roll.

specials.name: Keen Eyed
specials.description: An elf can see far better than the common man. As such he can spot hidden enemies at twice his Initiative value.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any good warband may hire a Wood Elf Hunter.

specials.name: Dark Magic
specials.description: The Sorceress is a wizard with two spells, rolled at random from Dark Elf Magic.

hire_fee.note: Free to hire before a battle. Afterwards the warband pays half of its earnings in gold crowns, rounding up, in tax.

upkeep_fee.note: Half of the warband's earnings in gold crowns, rounding up, after each battle, and 70 gc more if he came to harm.

hired_sword.unique_to: Dark Elf Corsairs only, as one of the Black Ark's Specialists.

specials.name: Cold One Beasthounds
specials.description: Two Cold One Beasthounds come with the Beastmaster: M6 WS3 BS0 S4 T4 W1 I1 A1 Ld4. A Beasthound causes fear and is subject to stupidity, and may use the Beastmaster's Leadership while within 6" of him. Its scaly skin gives it a 6+ armour save that may not be modified.

hire_fee.note: Free to hire before a battle. Afterwards the warband pays half of its earnings in gold crowns, rounding up, in tax.

upkeep_fee.note: Half of the warband's earnings in gold crowns, rounding up, after each battle, and 110 gc more if he came to harm.

hired_sword.unique_to: Dark Elf Corsairs only, as one of the Black Ark's Specialists.

specials.name: Frenzy
specials.description: The Witch Elf takes drugs before a battle and is subject to frenzy.

specials.name: Martial Arts
specials.description: The Witch Elf has a 5+ save against every wound she suffers.

hire_fee.note: Free to hire before a battle. Afterwards the warband pays half of its earnings in gold crowns, rounding up, in tax.

upkeep_fee.note: Half of the warband's earnings in gold crowns, rounding up, after each battle, and 50 gc more if he came to harm.

hired_sword.unique_to: Dark Elf Corsairs only, as one of the Black Ark's Specialists.

name: Ogre Treasure Hunter
description: Rum-soaked ogre treasure hunters have sailed the high seas living the life of a pirate. Sea-dogs are haulage dealers and deep-sea divers, salvagers of maritime paraphernalia who dive off shipwrecks to collect trinkets, hoarding every piece of junk they ensnare along the way.

specials.name: Diver
specials.description: The Ogre Treasure Hunter's rusty diving gear lets him move and breathe in water without penalty. He counts as aquatic.

specials.name: Fear
specials.description: Ogres are large, threatening creatures that cause fear.

specials.name: Large Target
specials.description: Ogres are Large Targets as defined in the shooting rules.

specials.name: Parrot Gnoblar
specials.description: The ogre is accompanied by a gnoblar dressed as a parrot, a claimed gnoblar represented on the ogre model. If the Ogre Treasure Hunter was not taken out of action, roll on the Cargo chart after each battle to see what salvage he swiped for the warband.

specials.name: Scrap-Dealer
specials.description: A warband with an Ogre Treasure Hunter can arrange trade deals with other warbands without a wagon or other vehicle. A vehicle is still required to benefit from a reputation in trade deals.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband with a riverboat or a barge except Skaven

name: Grave Warden
description: The priests of Morr cannot tend every Garden of Morr themselves, so Grave Wardens keep the grounds, walls and monuments, and patrol the perimeter against grave robbers, would-be necromancers and crypt ghouls. A Warden stands as the first line of defence against any unquiet undead.

specials.name: Immune to Disease
specials.description: A Grave Warden is not affected by any disease.

specials.name: Hardened
specials.description: Grave Wardens are immune to fear.

specials.name: Gardener
specials.description: A Grave Warden must move towards the nearest model that attacked a grave marker, or trespassed in a tomb, if he has line of sight. He hates all models defiling graves and charges any trespassers.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any Dwarf, Elf or Human warband

name: Halfling Fence
description: Not just anybody can run a fencing operation under the protection of the gangs that hire him. Halfling counterfeiters keep a low profile while they network independently of the racketeers in the city's underbelly.

specials.name: Sham
specials.description: Every item bought through the Fence is at its base price, with no random gold modifier, and at half that price. Once such an item is first used, roll a D6: on a 1 it breaks and is useless, an elaborate fake. At the end of each battle, whether or not the Fence took part, roll a D6 for what he has come by: 1 a Halfling cookbook, 2 an Ithilmar weapon, 3 a Gromril weapon, 4 a Tome of Magic or a Holy Tome, 5 a hunting rifle or an Elf bow, 6 a brace of duelling pistols.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband except Skaven, Undead, Beastmen and Orcs & Goblins

name: Halfling Pimp
description: Halfling agents make a career as sleazy expeditors in the seedier parts of the city, underworld guides and herders of harlots with delusional aspirations of becoming slave traffickers.

specials.name: Underworld Contacts
specials.description: A Hero visiting a bordello, a casino, a dream parlour or another Infamous Haunt while accompanied by a Pimp the warband has hired may re-roll any dice he rolls there. The second result must always be accepted.

specials.name: Flesh-peddler
specials.description: At the start of each battle nominate one of your opponent's female warriors as the Pimp's mark. Treat this as a Bounty Hunter's mark, except that the mark is captured by the Pimp instead of earning a reward after the battle. The Pimp has +1 to hit his mark and must always move towards her. He gains +D3 Experience for each mark he puts out of action if he survives and the battle was won. Do not roll on the Serious Injuries chart after the battle: marks count as captured, and any weapons may be kept by the warband or sold.

specials.name: Playboy
specials.description: A mark works for the Pimp's warband as a Courtesan and must always remain within 8" of him.

specials.name: Courtesans
specials.description: If the Pimp is taken out of action and none of his warband is within 8", his marks run for the nearest table edge in the hope of returning to their original warband. A mark that comes within 8" of its original warband is instantly controlled by the original owner. If the Pimp is taken out of action while a mark is within 8" of another warrior of his warband, the mark charges the closest model of that warband in range; treat the mark as having hatred.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband except Skaven, Undead, Beastmen and Orcs & Goblins

name: Albino Stormvermin
description: Hulking white-furred armoured mutes are Skavenblight's elite Stormvermin. Albino guard are granted sparingly, sent only to protect minions carrying out their dastardly assignments.

specials.name: Hardened
specials.description: The Council's bodyguard are chosen for their strength and relative fearlessness. They are immune to fear.

hired_sword.unique_to: Skaven warbands only

name: Bearman Bodyguard
description: Norse retainers are all the fashion with the nobility. Norscan mercenaries from Ormsgard and Urslo serve numerous Merchant Houses, and thirsty bodyguards are always garrisoned away from strong ale, food stores and women.

specials.name: Shieldmaster
specials.description: A Bearman Bodyguard may parry with his shield in addition to getting a saving throw.

specials.name: Drunken
specials.description: Roll a D6 at the start of each turn. On a 1 he must test for stupidity that turn; on a 2-5 nothing happens; on a 6 he is subject to frenzy for that turn. While subject to stupidity or frenzy he is immune to all other forms of psychology.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband except Undead and Skaven

name: Whaler
description: Whaling is an important trade for Norsca, and whalers are respected even among the warriors. Norscan whale-hunters sailing out of Marienburg must be made of sterner stuff than ordinary fishermen, and some sell their services as mercenaries in dangerous locales.

specials.name: Marine Hunter
specials.description: Double any wounds the Whaler inflicts on aquatic models.

specials.name: Hardened
specials.description: The Whaler is immune to fear.

specials.name: Harpooner
specials.description: When the Whaler hits and wounds a model in the shooting phase he may try to reel in the catch: if he passes a Strength test the target is pulled 8" towards him. Neither model counts as charging if the target is reeled into close combat.

specials.name: Whalebone Carver
specials.description: While a Whaler is with the warband, Heroes have +2 on search rolls for Scrimshaw Baubles.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband except Undead and Skaven

name: Fire-eater
description: Fire-eaters of Ind, Cathay and the Ogre Kingdoms are entertainers and assassins both, letting loose a belch of fire that curses foes as hair and hemp fry. What starts as a show can end in a dangerous explosion. Hired by Ogre Maneaters he has Movement 6.

specials.name: Fire-Stick
specials.description: In the shooting phase the Fire-Eater spits fire upon his enemies. Use the teardrop flame template to see which models suffer an automatic Strength 4 hit, and any model hit is set on fire on a roll of 4+. He can use this breath attack even while engaged in close combat.

specials.name: Inhaling Fire
specials.description: After the first flume, roll a D6 each time the Fire-Eater makes another breath attack. On a 1 he has inhaled the fire he should have been spewing and suffers a Strength 4 hit instead of using the template.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any Human warband, the Battle Monks of Cathay, and Ogre Maneaters (with Movement 6)

name: Sister of Sigmar
description: The Sisters of Sigmar have traditionally travelled the Empire tending to orphans, and their advice is sought by those about to make an important decision. Their popularity wanes as Witch Hunters denounce them as witches, but Wastelanders see them as anything but heretics.

specials.name: Blessing of Sigmar
specials.description: The Sister has two of the Sisters of Sigmar special skills.

specials.name: Candle Tree
specials.description: Her Arcane Candelabrum counts as a holy relic, a brazier iron and a lantern, and is used one-handed. Any mutant taken out of action by the Sister of Sigmar is captured.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any Dwarf, Elf or Human warband except Witch Hunters

name: Midshipman
description: Amidst the winding channels linking the River Reik to the Manaanspoort Sea, many Midshipmen lend their services to a warband willing to pay. Hardened by years at sea, they can rouse the most shambolic of men into a crew of reasonable aptitude.

specials.name: A Crew Fer Me!
specials.description: A Midshipman craves the comradery and adventure of the sea and a worthy crew, so any seafaring warband has +1 to its blood pact rolls with him.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband except Skaven, Beastmen and Orcs & Goblins

name: Bog Hunter
description: Some men have lost so much, or want such strange things, that they have been shunned from normal society, and a few have befriended the creatures of the swamp. They work almost as slaves for the monsters, acting as spies and errand-runners in the human world. He may also learn the Academic skills Streetwise and Haggle.

specials.name: Unholy Stink
specials.description: The Bog Hunter is covered in a thick layer of dung, and the smell is so distracting that all enemies are at -1 to hit him in close combat.

specials.name: Gopher
specials.description: In place of a Hero's roll on either the Daemon Swamp or Trading, the Bog Hunter may visit any one place in the Craftsmarket, the Infamous Haunts or the Marketplace while the Hero waits outside town for his return.

specials.name: Fenland Strider
specials.description: The Bog Hunter may re-roll any failed Initiative test while fighting on causeways, jetties and gangplanks, or crossing a marsh.

hired_sword.unique_to: Fimir, Beastmen and Greenskin warbands

name: Lisette Leerer
description: Saleswoman and enforcer for the League of Gentlemen Entrepreneurs, the most powerful crime organisation in the Free City of Marienburg.

specials.name: Iron Amulet
specials.description: Her amulet uses the natural properties of metal to resist magic: any spell that would target the area of the wearer has its casting difficulty increased by 2.

specials.name: League Business
specials.description: Roll a D6 for every rare item the warband gets hold of whose rarity is at least Rare 12. On a 1 the item is appropriated by the League of Gentlemen Entrepreneurs.

specials.name: Guild Membership
specials.description: Lisette is an appointed enforcer protected by the Marienburg Gentleman's Club. She may not be placed under arrest.

specials.name: Protection Racket
specials.description: Any human Hired Sword the warband encounters through a random happening or an exploration result may join a warband Lisette accompanies. The player may not actively hire a Hired Sword the warband could not normally hire. Such a Hired Sword may only be removed from the roster if his upkeep is not paid, if he dies from being taken out of action, or if an enemy model has captured him.

hire_fee.note: D3+1 Treasures or wyrdstone shards after each game she took part in.

upkeep_fee.note: Her hire fee is paid after each game she took part in.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband except Skaven

name: Trancas Quendalmanliye
description: A Wood Elf charlatan who keeps the casino door, and a wizard's apprentice turned gambler.

specials.name: Wizard
specials.description: Trancas was a wizard's apprentice and has two spells generated at random from the Lesser Magic list.

specials.name: Songster
specials.description: Any friendly model within 6" of Trancas may re-roll a failed Leadership test with +1 Leadership. This includes Rout tests.

specials.name: Pick Locks
specials.description: When testing to open a locked door, Trancas only needs to make an Initiative test.

specials.name: Hate Orcs and Dark Elves
specials.description: Trancas hates Orcs and Goblins, and Dark Elves as well.

specials.name: Amulet of Thrice-Blessed Copper
specials.description: On a successful Toughness test Trancas is unaffected by any poison attack. Non-magical weapons inflict 1 Wound less when he is attacked in hand-to-hand combat.

hire_fee.note: A quarter of all gold crowns earned after each game he took part in. Wyrdstone shards and treasures found must all be sold after the battle to work out his fee.

upkeep_fee.note: His hire fee is paid after each game he took part in.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband except Skaven and Undead

name: Sam Warble
description: The diminutive sleuth is famous for solving Marienburgers' problems for the right price, delving into suspicious characters and uncovering secrets. With a network of more informants than anyone else in the city, Sam Warble can find anything or anyone at a price.

specials.name: Bribery
specials.description: Sam Warble can never be placed under arrest. Any warrior being placed or already placed under arrest can be released without rolling on the Conviction chart by paying a bribe.

specials.name: Jack of All Trades
specials.description: Sam may use any item or weapon he encounters and wear any cloak or armour, and equipment may be bought for him as for any other member of the warband. Any weapon given to Sam is his to keep: he will not pass it to another member later.

specials.name: Night Vision
specials.description: In an underground scenario Sam spots hidden enemies from twice his Initiative value in inches away.

specials.name: Sixth Sense
specials.description: Once per game Sam may choose the result of any dice roll he makes, but not one made by another member of the warband.

specials.name: Stealthy
specials.description: Sam can hide even after running, and can run while within 8" of enemy models if he starts and ends his move hidden.

specials.name: True Detective
specials.description: A warrior taken out of action in close combat by Sam Warble is placed under arrest whenever the injury roll on a D6 is 5-6, unless Sam's warband routed. Equipment belonging to a warrior placed under arrest cannot be kept by the warband unless it was impounded under the campaign's objectives, and confiscated items cannot be sold or traded.

specials.name: Private Eye
specials.description: At the start of each battle nominate one of your opponent's warriors as Sam's mark. Treat this as a Bounty Hunter's mark, except that the mark is placed under arrest instead of earning a reward after the battle. Sam has +1 to hit his mark and must always move towards him.

hire_fee.note: 30 gc after the first game he took part in, and 15 gc more for each later assignment with the same warband. If more than one player wants him, and the campaign's objectives do not say otherwise, he goes to the highest bidder.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband except Skaven, Undead, Beastmen and Orcs & Goblins

specials.name: Always Goes to Battle
specials.description: The Seer always accompanies the warband into battle.

specials.name: Never Armoured
specials.description: The model never wears armour.

specials.name: No Heavy Weapons
specials.description: The Seer may not use a double-handed weapon or a shield.

specials.name: Reading
specials.description: At the beginning of each battle every hero in the warband may ask the Seer for a single reading; he does not have to. A hero within 6" of the Seer may instead ask for a reading during the battle: it costs double, 10 gc, and the result applies from the beginning of the following Seer player's turn. A reading's effects last for one battle.

specials.name: Cards of Fortune
specials.description:
Each result is the card the Seer picks. Roll two differently coloured D6: one for the column, one for the row.

Columns: 1 Circle of Life (health); 2-3 Leaf of Fortune (good luck); 4-5 Stone of Riches (wealth); 6 Spear of Misfortune (bad luck).

Twins (1-2)
Circle of Life - Tough: the hero may force an opponent to re-roll a single injury roll made against him.
Leaf of Fortune - Lucky: the hero may re-roll any one of his own dice during the battle, never an opponent's.
Stone of Riches - Finders Keepers: the hero finds a stash of 2D6 gc in the exploration phase, if he was not taken out of action.
Spear of Misfortune - Unlucky: the enemy player may force the hero to re-roll a single dice during the game.

Servant (3)
Circle of Life - Hard Nut: once per battle, the hero is knocked down instead of stunned.
Leaf of Fortune - Very Lucky: the hero may adjust a single dice by 1 in the exploration phase, if he was not taken out of action.
Stone of Riches - Money Pouch: the hero finds 2D6+5 gc in the exploration phase, if he was not taken out of action.
Spear of Misfortune - Poor Hunting: the enemy player may adjust a single dice rolled for the warband in the exploration phase by 1. It must always be to the warband's harm.

Mother (4)
Circle of Life - Impervious to Pain: the hero may ignore the first wound he suffers during the battle.
Leaf of Fortune - You're So Clumsy: the hero may name a single enemy warrior within 12" at any time during the battle. The next time that warrior moves, he must roll under his Initiative on a D6 or trip and count as knocked down.
Stone of Riches - Jewellery Box: the hero finds jewellery worth 2D6+10 gc in the exploration phase, if he was not taken out of action.
Spear of Misfortune - Accident Prone: roll a D6 each turn the hero moves. On a 6 he falls over and counts as knocked down.

Father (5)
Circle of Life - Constitution of an Ox: once per battle, the hero is knocked down instead of stunned or taken out of action.
Leaf of Fortune - Butterfingers: the hero may name a single enemy warrior within 12" at any time during the battle. That warrior at once drops one weapon, chosen by the hero. If he is in combat and wins the round he may recover it; if he loses, it is lost. A warrior not in combat may recover it at the end of his turn, and may not fire a missile weapon that turn.
Stone of Riches - Lady's Loss: the hero finds a coronet worth 3D6+20 gc in the exploration phase, if he was not taken out of action.
Spear of Misfortune - Poor Morale: the warband loses faith in its leader. He loses the Leader rule for the rest of the battle.

Spirit (6)
Circle of Life - Charmed Life: the hero may force an opponent to re-roll every to-wound roll made against him during the battle.
Leaf of Fortune - Family Loyalty: the hero may add one henchman to any henchmen group or start a new group with him. He is armed with a single-handed weapon or a missile weapon that is not a black powder weapon, and a dagger. This may take the warband over its maximum.
Stone of Riches - Hero's Loss: the hero finds a crown worth 6D6+20 gc in the exploration phase, if he was not taken out of action.
Spear of Misfortune - Desertion: a single henchman of the player's choice who is not out of action, stunned or knocked down deserts the warband, catches a fatal disease or is otherwise lost. Remove him from the roster; the warband may not keep his equipment.

specials.name: Curse
specials.description: If the Seer dies, roll a D6 at once for each hero in the warband and for the warrior who took her out of action. On a 4+ that warrior suffers an effect from the Spear of Misfortune column: roll a D6 for the row and apply it. If she is dismissed, the warband's leader has to test unless he pays her off with 8D6 gc, or 6D6 gc if he has the Haggle skill.

hire_fee.note: No hire fee: she takes a retainer of 15 gc before each battle.

upkeep_fee.note: 5 gc for each reading, and 10 gc for a reading made during the battle.

hired_sword.unique_to: Only human and Vampire warbands may hire a Strigany Seer.

specials.name: Chosen Weapons
specials.description: The Assassin starts with one of: fighting claws with either one dose of Black Lotus or one dose of Dark Venom; weeping blades; or a sword, a dagger and a blowpipe. He always has light armour and a helmet.

specials.name: No Two Together
specials.description: An established Clan Eshin warband will not hire a freelance Assassin, and two Assassins will never fight for the same warband, even if one of them is sent on an assassination.

specials.name: Perfect Killer
specials.description: Every attack the model makes, shooting or in close combat, has an extra -1 save modifier.

specials.name: Disengage (Clan Eshin Assassin)
specials.description: At the beginning of his turn the Assassin may leave combat without his opponent getting a free hit, provided he is fighting a single enemy warrior. Fighting two or more, he may not leave combat. A model knocked down or stunned does not count as being in combat.

specials.name: Assassinate
specials.description: Instead of taking part in a battle, the Assassin may be hired to take out the opposition. The warband names an enemy hero. When the enemy warband deploys, the Assassin is already lying in wait: he charges the named hero and the two fight one round of combat, after which the Assassin leaves the battlefield whatever the result. He automatically surprises his target and always strikes first, whatever weapon the target carries. The attempt happens immediately before the first turn of the battle.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any Skaven warband except Clan Eshin may hire a Clan Eshin Assassin.

name: Clan Skryre Engineer
description: Also carries: a warp-glaive and a trained rat familiar.

specials.name: Tinkerer
specials.description:
While the warband has a Clan Skryre Engineer it must use the misfire rules from the back of the Mordheim rulebook. The Engineer may tinker with pistols of any kind, handguns and jezzails. Each time a warrior in the warband fires such an upgraded weapon and rolls a 1 to hit, do not roll on the normal misfire chart; roll a D6 on this one instead.

D6 | Effect
1 | Boom! The shot explodes in the barrel. The shooter suffers a S4 hit, which causes no critical hits, and the weapon is destroyed.
2-3 | Jammed. The bullet is stuck in the barrel and the weapon may not be fired again this battle. It is cleared in time for the next battle.
4-5 | Phut. The black powder fails to ignite. The warrior may try to fire again next turn.
6 | Ka-Boom! The upgrade works better than planned: the shot's Strength is increased by 1.

specials.name: Warp-Glaive
specials.description: A halberd with a warpstone chamber at the base of the blade. Range close combat, Strength as user +2, two-handed and unstable. Two-handed: a model using it may not use a shield, buckler or additional hand weapon in close combat; with a shield he still gets +1 to his armour save against shooting. Unstable: on a natural 1 to wound, the wielder takes a S3 hit that ignores armour saves, the coils burn out and the glaive counts as a halberd (S+1) for the rest of the battle. It costs 45 gc, rarity 10, and only the Engineer may use it.

specials.name: Upgrades
specials.description:
A warband with a Clan Skryre Engineer may buy these upgrades for its weapons.

Targeter, 15 gc, rarity 9: the shooter gets +1 BS.
Extra strong warpstone ammunition, 25 gc, rarity 10: the weapon gets +1 S, but misfires on a roll of 1-2.
Trained rat familiar, 30 gc, rarity 10: the rat recharges the weapon, so the warrior may shoot each turn as if with a brace. It works with every weapon that needs reloading, and gives no benefit to a warrior who already has a brace.
Increased barrel, 40 gc, rarity 9: the weapon's range grows by D6", rolled once per battle.
Ratling gun, 200 gc, rarity 11: range 12", Strength 4 with a -2 save modifier, move or fire, multiple shots, barrel-carrier. Barrel-carrier: two warriors must handle it, one holding the gun and one the barrel. Multiple shots: name the target and roll a dice; the result is how many shots you get, and you may keep rolling further dice for more shots as often as you like. If you ever roll the same result twice, consult the ratling gun misfire chart: double 1s or 2s, no shots are fired; double 3s or 4s, it shoots in a random direction, rolled with 2D6 for the distance and the artillery dice for the direction, and the first model in its path is hit; double 5s or 6s, it explodes, both warriors handling it are automatically out of action and every other warrior within 2" takes a S4 hit.

hired_sword.unique_to: Only Skaven warbands may hire a Clan Skryre Engineer.

specials.name: Fear
specials.description: The model causes fear.

specials.name: Immune to Psychology
specials.description: The model is immune to psychology and never leaves combat.

specials.name: Immune to Poison
specials.description: Not affected by any poison.

specials.name: May Not Run
specials.description: The model may not run, but may charge normally.

specials.name: Chill Touch
specials.description: The Reaper's attacks ignore armour.

specials.name: Ethereal (Reaper)
specials.description: The Reaper may move through solid objects such as walls at will, but may not end his move inside one, and may not move through living beings. He cannot charge an enemy he cannot see.

specials.name: Hard to Hit
specials.description: All shots at the Reaper are at -1 to hit. He may also take a Leadership test to avoid taking a wound. He gets no special save against magical attacks.

specials.name: Combat Resolution
specials.description: The Reaper suffers no wounds from attacks themselves. When a combat involving him is finished, total the difference in wounds caused by each side, adding 1 if more than one enemy attacked him. If he suffered more wounds than the enemy, he must take a Leadership test with a penalty equal to that total. If he fails, he suffers a wound; with no wounds left he automatically goes out of action. He can never be knocked down or stunned.

specials.name: Disrupted Essence
specials.description: When the Reaper is put out of action he does not roll on the Serious Injury chart. He must return to his crypt and misses the next battle. Roll a D6: on a 1 he has failed to recover and is laid to rest for good.

specials.name: Maximum Profile
specials.description: The Reaper gains experience as other hired swords do, and his maximum profile is a human's.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any Undead warband may hire a Reaper.

available_special_skills.name: Combat Master
available_special_skills.description: The Reaper has the Combat Master skill.

available_special_skills.name: Expert Scyther
available_special_skills.description: As Expert Swordsman, but for the Reaper's scythe instead of a sword.

available_special_skills.name: Sorcery
available_special_skills.description: If the Reaper has his Arcane Lore skill, he gets +1 to his rolls to cast spells.

available_special_skills.name: Arcane Lore (Reaper)
available_special_skills.description: The Reaper may learn Necromancy from his personal spellbook.

available_special_skills.name: Death's Strength
available_special_skills.description: The Reaper ignores the usual penalty of always striking last with his scythe; work out the order of combat as with other weapons.

available_special_skills.name: Death's Haste
available_special_skills.description: If the Reaper is charged, the order of attack is worked out by comparing Initiative instead of the charger striking first.

specials.name: Starting Skills
specials.description: The Halfling Thief starts with Eagle Eyes or Quick Shot, and with one of his own thief skills.

specials.name: Small
specials.description: The Halfling Thief may not use double-handed weapons, bows other than short bows, or any black powder weapon.

hired_sword.unique_to: Only 'good' warbands (human, High Elf, Wood Elf and Dwarf) may hire a Halfling Thief.

available_special_skills.name: Thieving
available_special_skills.description: At the end of a game, if he did not go out of action, the Thief may try to steal a single item he could normally use. Roll 2D6: a non-rare item is stolen on a 4+; a rare item needs a roll over (not equal to) its rarity, and a 12 always succeeds. On a failure he has been Sold to the Pits (65 on the heroes' Serious Injury chart).

available_special_skills.name: Pick Pocket
available_special_skills.description: Instead of attacking, the Thief may try to take an item from an enemy warrior in base contact at the beginning of a round of combat. The item may be anything up to the size of a single-handed weapon, but not one worn or held in the enemy's hands. For money, a henchman carries 5% of the warband's total wealth and a hero 10%, up to the warband's total; the rest is out of reach. He must declare what he is stealing and pass an Initiative test, where a 6 always fails. On a success he may not attack that round but may use the item from the beginning of the next turn, even the enemy's. On a failure every hit against him strikes on a 3+ and he goes last in that round of combat, for that round only. A Thief with this skill within 2" of a disarmed enemy may pick the weapon up at once without an Initiative test, but may do nothing else that turn.

available_special_skills.name: Trap Expert
available_special_skills.description: The Thief never sets off a trap himself, though he may suffer from one that goes off near him. He may try to disarm a trap he comes upon: he must stop at it in his movement and do nothing else that turn, then roll 2D6, needing 6+ for a simple trap or 8+ for a complex one. On a failure he must roll against his own Initiative, and a failed test means he has set the trap off. He may also restore a dud or disarmed trap: roll a D6 for what a dud becomes, 1-4 simple and 5-6 complex, while a disarmed trap returns to what it was, then roll 2D6, needing 6+ for a simple trap or 8+ for a complex one.

available_special_skills.name: Hide In Shadows
available_special_skills.description: An enemy warrior trying to detect the hidden Thief must halve his Initiative before measuring the distance.

available_special_skills.name: Backstabbing
available_special_skills.description: If the Thief is undetected by an enemy within his normal movement of 4", he may charge him in his turn, 6" with the Sprint skill. When he charges this way he adds 1 to his Strength and his enemy loses one attack, in the first round of combat only.

name: Prospector (Karak Azgal)
description: The row is the human Prospector; the page also gives a Dwarf Prospector, whose hire fee, upkeep, rating and profile are in the fee notes. A Dwarf Prospector may also take Dwarf skills.

specials.name: Crossbow for a Dwarf
specials.description: A human Prospector carries a bow; a Dwarf Prospector carries a crossbow instead.

hire_fee.note: A Dwarf Prospector costs 30 gc to hire, and has the Dwarf profile: M3 WS4 BS3 S3 T4 W1 I2 A1 Ld9.

upkeep_fee.note: A Dwarf Prospector costs 20 gc upkeep, and raises the warband's rating by 20 points plus 1 for each experience point.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any Dwarf or human warband may hire a Prospector.

available_special_skills.name: Luck (Prospector)
available_special_skills.description: The Prospector may re-roll a single dice in the game. He starts with this skill and may learn it twice more, for up to three re-rolls in a game. A re-roll not used during a battle may be used on a single dice in the post-battle sequence, exploration dice and his own serious injury included.

available_special_skills.name: Prospector
available_special_skills.description: If the Prospector was not taken out of action he may go prospecting as well as exploring normally, and finds a further D6-1 gc for the warband.

available_special_skills.name: Loner
available_special_skills.description: The Prospector never takes All Alone tests.

specials.name: Necromantic Magic
specials.description: The Necromancer is a wizard who uses Necromantic magic. He starts with the spells Awakening and Death Vision. When he would gain a new skill he may instead roll a new spell from the Necromantic spell list at random.

hired_sword.unique_to: Clan Pestilens, Blood Dragons, Marienburgers, Dark Elf Raiders, a Strigoi warband or the Brigands may hire the Necromancer.

name: Grave Robber (Mousillon)
description: Also carries a shovel, a pick and a pry bar, which have no effect in the game.

specials.name: Familiar with the Crypts
specials.description: The warband may change a single dice roll on the Exploration chart by 1 either way.

specials.name: Trap Expert
specials.description: The Grave Robber has the Trap Expert skill.

hired_sword.unique_to: Clan Pestilens, Blood Dragons, Marienburgers, Dark Elf Raiders, a Strigoi warband or the Brigands may hire the Grave Robber.

specials.name: My God Is With Me
specials.description: The Priest never needs to take All Alone tests.

specials.name: Purification
specials.description: While a warband uses a Priest of Morr, no dead warrior of that warband may ever be raised to undeath by the Spell of Awakening, turned into a zombie as a sacrifice, or raised to undeath by any other means.

specials.name: Poor
specials.description: The Priest comes armed only with a dagger. When he is hired the warband may give him a sword, a club or a scythe (a halberd) that it has, or buy one for him. If he ever leaves the warband, by death, failure to pay upkeep or otherwise, that weapon is lost with him, and it may not be traded from then on.

specials.name: Rituals of Morr
specials.description: The Priest may perform ancient Rituals of Morr, which count as prayers in every respect. He begins with two, determined at random. When he gains an advance he may gain a new Ritual instead of a skill.

spells.name: 1 - Morr's Protection
spells.description: Difficulty 7. Any magical attack or prayer made by a spellcaster or priest who is not of Morr, and which would be a direct attack on the Priest, is negated on a 4+. While the protection lasts, a damaging spell may never put the Priest out of action: treat an out of action result as stunned. The prayer stays in play until it successfully saves against such an attack.

spells.name: 2 - Death Holds No Fear
spells.description: Difficulty 6. The Priest is immune to fear. Undead and chaos beings within 6" must pass a Leadership test each combat phase or lose one attack, which can never reduce them to no attacks. They test even though they are immune to psychology, because this tests the will that holds them together. The Priest must pass a Leadership test at the start of his magic phases or the prayer ends.

spells.name: 3 - Sanctity From the Fallen
spells.description: Difficulty 7. Every friendly model within 6" gets +1 to its armour save, and a 6+ save where it had none. Any undead model, or any creature tainted by chaos, is at -1 to hit those warriors.

spells.name: 4 - Hand of Morr
spells.description: Difficulty 9. One undead model in base contact with the Priest, a vampire, dire wolf, zombie or skeleton among them, goes out of action. A ghoul or chaos-tainted character he touches flees its full movement away from him. Every other character strikes last in the next round of combat.

spells.name: 5 - Presence of Morr
spells.description: Difficulty 8. Any one ordinary model within 6" of the Priest suffers an automatic wound with no save allowed. A chaotic being is at +1 on the injury table if it is reduced to no wounds. The rite causes 2 wounds on an undead creature, and adds 1 to any injury rolls for it.

spells.name: 6 - I Am Death!
spells.description: Difficulty 9. The Priest fights with Weapon Skill 4 and +1 Attack, and gains a 6+ unmodifiable ward save. He must pass a Leadership test at the start of his magic phases or the prayer ends.

hired_sword.unique_to: Human warbands not associated with Chaos or Undead may hire a Priest of Morr. He may work alongside priests of another religion, though it is unusual.

specials.name: Alchemist
specials.description: The Alchemist knows two potion recipes, determined at random, when he is hired. When he gains a new skill he may instead learn a new recipe, determined at random; roll again for a duplicate.

specials.name: Potions (Alchemist)
specials.description: Potions are the results of the recipes the Alchemist knows. They are all used at the start of the battle, the exploding potion aside, and thrown potions follow the rules for thrown weapons. A potion lasts for one battle and is then useless. Before the battle the Alchemist may make potions from two different recipes he knows, D3-1 potions from each. If he uses a potion on himself or his own equipment he never suffers its bad consequences. If another warrior suffers from a potion, the Alchemist will refuse to make any further potions for him.

specials.name: Potion Recipes
specials.description:
1. Potion of Flames. Used on one weapon, which counts as +1 Strength. A creature susceptible to fire suffers 2 wounds instead of one. After the battle roll a D6: on a 1 the weapon is burnt and worthless.
2. Leather Skin Potion. The drinker's skin gives a 5+ armour save, which may not be modified beyond 6+. It cannot be used while he wears body armour, but may be combined with a shield. After the battle roll a D6: on a 1 the skin tears and he must roll on the Serious Injury table, rolling again for death, capture and sold to the pits.
3. Muscle Potion. The drinker is +1 Strength for the rest of the battle, which may take him beyond his racial maximum. After the battle roll a D6: on a 1 he is -1 Strength for the next battle.
4. Exploding Potion. Thrown, and explodes on its target with a S5 hit. If it misses it rolls D3" in a random direction and explodes there; on a 1 to hit it goes D3" in a random direction from the thrower. Everything within 1" of the explosion takes a S3 hit.
5. Berserker Potion. The drinker becomes frenzied. After the battle roll a D6: on a 1 he is too ill to fight and misses the next battle.
6. Potion of Speed. Rubbed on one warrior's legs and arms, he is +1 Movement and +1 Initiative for the battle. Drunk instead, his Initiative becomes 10 and his Movement 6, but he falls ill and misses the next game. The Alchemist will never drink it himself.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband not opposed to the use of gunpowder may hire the Alchemist.

available_special_skills.name: Adept Potionmaker
available_special_skills.description: The Alchemist may make one more potion of a recipe he knows before the battle. This may let him take three different potions to battle instead of two.

available_special_skills.name: Powder and Gun Specialist
available_special_skills.description: One black powder weapon per game may add 6" to its range and hit at +1 Strength. This cannot be combined with the Hunter skill, and the black powder misfire table becomes compulsory.

specials.name: Fear
specials.description: The model causes fear.

specials.name: Spells of Wrath
specials.description: The Dark Maiden is a wizard and uses the Spells of Wrath. She starts with two of them, determined at random. When she gains a new skill she may instead roll on the Spells of Wrath list.

spells.name: 1 - Dark Strength
spells.description: Difficulty 8. The Dark Maiden may pick herself or any one friendly model within 6". That model gains +1 Attack and scores a critical hit on a 5+. The spell lasts until the beginning of her next magic or shooting phase.

spells.name: 2 - Ebony Blade
spells.description: Difficulty 6. The Dark Maiden enchants one bladed weapon within 6". It gains +1 to the injury roll, and if it hits, its victim is -1 Toughness until the end of the next combat turn. The enchantment lasts for one turn of combat.

spells.name: 3 - Black Lightning
spells.description: Difficulty 7. Choose a target in sight within 12". It suffers a S4 hit. If that causes a wound, D3 S2 hits strike models within 6", one hit per model at most.

spells.name: 4 - Dark Infuse
spells.description: Difficulty 6. A single model within 2", the Dark Maiden included, regains 1 lost wound. He stands up at once and may fight that round at +1 Strength, in normal order.

spells.name: 5 - Purple Aura
spells.description: Difficulty 7. Every model within 6" of the Dark Maiden, herself included, gets +1 Weapon Skill and +1 Initiative. A friendly model within 6" that has just recovered from being knocked down comes to its senses and fights as normal, so does not strike last.

spells.name: 6 - Cold Shadow
spells.description: Difficulty 8. One visible target within 12" loses a wound unless it passes a Strength test, and keeps losing one each round until it passes. A model that loses its last wound, or has already lost it, rolls on the injury chart.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband may use the Dark Maiden, so long as it has no White Lady or other law-enforcing hired sword.

specials.name: Herald of the Lady
specials.description: The White Lady will never work in a warband that already employs any other magic user, any assassin or a grave robber.

specials.name: Spells of the Lake
specials.description: The White Lady is a wizard and uses the Spells of the Lake. She starts with one of them, determined at random. When she gains a new skill she may instead roll on the Spells of the Lake list.

spells.name: 1 - Early Morning Fog
spells.description: Difficulty 8. Anyone shooting at the White Lady, or at any friendly model within 6", is at -1 to hit. Models in the mist suffer no critical hits. The spell lasts until the beginning of her next magic or shooting phase.

spells.name: 2 - Blade of Ice
spells.description: Difficulty 7. The White Lady enchants one bladed weapon within 6". It gains +1 to hit, and if it hits, its victim automatically strikes last in the next round of combat. The enchantment lasts for one round of combat.

spells.name: 3 - Intangible Like the Mist
spells.description: Difficulty 7. The White Lady may pick herself or any one friendly model within 6". That model may charge without being intercepted and may discard the first hit it takes. The spell lasts until the beginning of her next magic or shooting phase.

spells.name: 4 - Three Drops of Fortune
spells.description: Difficulty 6. A single model within 2", the White Lady included, may re-roll D3 failed single dice rolls while he is blessed. The spell lasts until the beginning of her next turn.

spells.name: 5 - A Tear From the Lady
spells.description: Difficulty 5. Any one model within 2" of the White Lady, herself included, is restored to his full wounds. A friendly model within 2" that is stunned or knocked down also comes to its senses, stands up and fights as normal.

spells.name: 6 - Ice Gaze
spells.description: Difficulty 9. One visible target within 12" takes a S5 hit that causes D3 wounds. Any model within 2" of it takes a single S3 hit.

hired_sword.unique_to: Knight Errant, Brigand and Woodsmen warbands may hire the White Lady.

specials.name: Two Weapons of His Choosing
specials.description: The Frankain Mercenary carries two of these weapons: a sword, an axe, a morning star or a club. He fights only on foot.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband except Bretonnians may hire the Frankain Mercenary.

specials.name: Fear
specials.description: The model causes fear.

specials.name: Elemental Magic (Genie)
specials.description: A Genie is tied to one of the elements of water, fire, earth or air. Roll 2D6 when he is hired: 2-4 water, 5-6 fire, 7-8 air, 9-11 earth, 12 your choice. He may take spells from that element's list. He starts with one spell and one Genie power, and gains another when he advances.

specials.name: Genie Powers
specials.description:
A Genie may use one of these powers at the start of his turn, and it lasts until the end of his opponent's turn.

Whirlwind: the Genie may run at triple his Movement but may not charge or be charged. He may make no attacks of any kind while he does, and is at -1 to hit with missile weapons.
Genie's Curse: all of the Genie's enemies within 4" are at -1 to their to-hit rolls and all of their saves. This power is active throughout the whole battle.
Lucky: the Genie has an unmodifiable 5+ save against all hits.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband may hire a Genie.

specials.name: Club or Staff
specials.description: The Lazar carries either a club or a staff as well as his dagger and sling.

specials.name: Fear
specials.description: The model causes fear.

specials.name: Recognised on Sight
specials.description: The Lazar causes fear in all living races. Followers of Nurgle and of Clan Pestilens are not frightened by his appearance and are not afraid of catching his diseases.

specials.name: No Pain
specials.description: The model treats a stunned result on the Injury chart as knocked down.

specials.name: The Disease Advances
specials.description: The Lazar gains no skills. Instead his disease advances: any model within 1" of him must pass a psychology test or flee away from him, and that range grows by 1" for each further skill advance he rolls.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband that dares approach him may hire the Lazar.

name: Cartographer
description: Also carries a quarter map.

specials.name: Uncharted No More
specials.description: Whenever the warband plays a scenario in which the Cartographer has taken part at least once already, it may change the roll to see which warband sets up first by 1 either way.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any human warband except the Maidens of Dusk and Dawn may hire a Cartographer.

name: Clocked Crook
description: Also carries an in-built clockwork totem, which counts as a banner and a halberd.

specials.name: Construct
specials.description: A construct as the Clockworkers warband list describes.

specials.name: Gift of Sentience
specials.description: A Clocked crook has been given the Gift of Sentience and so ignores some of the constructs' usual rules.

specials.name: Countermeasures
specials.description: A Clocked crook counts as having the Rogue control skill.

specials.name: Moonstone Infusion
specials.description: A Clocked crook may learn the Clockworkers' special skill Moonstone infusion.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband except the Clockworkers may hire a Clocked crook.

name: Maiden Guide
description: Also carries a clockwork rifle.

specials.name: Native
specials.description: A Maiden guide counts as having the Archaeologist skill, and may learn the Academic skill Wyrdstone Hunter.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband which includes humans or Dwarfs may hire a Maiden guide.

specials.name: Fear
specials.description: The model causes fear.

specials.name: Huge Stamina
specials.description: The Ogre cannoneer ignores the swivel gun's Cumbersome rule.

specials.name: Large
specials.description: This unit is treated as a Large Target. They may always be shot at with ranged weapons with a +1 modifier to hit.

hired_sword.unique_to: Mercenaries and Pirates may hire an Ogre cannoneer.

specials.name: No Weapons
specials.description: A Reactivated archivist carries no weapons or armour.

specials.name: Collector
specials.description: If the Reactivated archivist was not taken out of action, the warband may re-roll a single dice in the exploration phase.

specials.name: Construct
specials.description: A construct as the Clockworkers warband list describes.

specials.name: Observer
specials.description: After each game the archivist may pass a Leadership test to grant the warband a single re-roll the next time it plays against the warband it has just fought. If the warband lost the game, the archivist passes the test automatically.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband with access to the fourth ring may hire a Reactivated archivist.

specials.name: Spear or Halberd
specials.description: The Warlock engineer carries a spear or a halberd as well as his dagger.

specials.name: Chain Lightning Only
specials.description: Warlock engineers count as spellcasters and know the Chain Lightning spell. They may not learn any other spell.

spells.name: Chain Lightning
spells.description: Difficulty 7. This spell cannot be cast while in hand-to-hand combat. It summons a bolt of green lightning with a range of 24", which the Warlock engineer shoots at one enemy model. Use his own Ballistic Skill to see whether he hits, but ignore movement, range and cover penalties. It causes one S3 hit with no armour save. After the hit is resolved roll a D6: on a 5+, or a 3+ if both models stand in the same water terrain, the bolt hits the closest model within 6" of the last target; on a 1 the Warlock engineer is hit instead. It may bounce several times, but each model may only be hit once per turn.

hired_sword.unique_to: Any warband which includes Skaven may hire a Warlock engineer.

available_special_skills.name: Supercharged Chain-Lightning Modulator
available_special_skills.description: The Warlock engineer may deliberately raise Chain Lightning's difficulty. For every 2 points of added difficulty, the spell's Strength is increased by 1 that turn.

available_special_skills.name: Upgraded Warp-Energy Condenser
available_special_skills.description: The Warlock engineer permanently lowers Chain Lightning's difficulty by D3-1 points. It may be taken more than once.

name: Jezzail Gunner
description: Also carries a scope. His profile is already reduced by the cannon's Cumbersome rule: before it he is M5 BS4 I4, and with the cannon M4 BS3(4 with the scope) I3.

specials.name: Homebound
specials.description: He is only found in the Sartosa campaign setting.

specials.name: Jezzail Cannon
specials.description: The Jezzail Cannon always uses the Move or Fire and Prepare Shot rules. It may never be fired twice in a turn, nor fired if the user moved, whatever skills he has. It is cumbersome, which reduces the carrier's Movement and Initiative by 1 each.

specials.name: Scope
specials.description: Most shots allow the use of the scope, and the warplock jezzail then fires at +1 Ballistic Skill.

specials.name: Shot
specials.description:
